correctness.rationale: Exchangeability gives the one-transition probability. Two adjacent transitions occur exactly in patterns 010 and 101, yielding joint probability \(ab/[N(N-1)]\). Two disjoint transitions use four distinct positions with two ones and two zeros in four orientations, yielding \(4a(a-1)b(b-1)/[N(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)]\). Subtracting the squared marginal gives the displayed factorizations. The disjoint zero equation would force \(2N-3\) to divide N because \(\gcd(2N-3,N-2)=1\), impossible for \(N\ge4\). Bernoulli zero covariance is independence, so adjacent independence is exactly \(d^2=N\), equivalent to the stated square-size compositions. Fresh exact enumeration independently verified all formulas for every nontrivial composition with 4 through 10 positions, 42 cases.

value.rationale: Transition indicators are the elementary constituents of the classical runs statistic. The exact sign phases reveal how positive and negative local associations cancel inside the familiar scalar variance and identify a non-obvious regime of adjacent independence coexisting with persistent negative disjoint dependence. That is a natural structural refinement of a standard statistic.

final_claim: For a uniformly random binary word with fixed counts a and b, adjacent and disjoint transition indicators have the stated exact covariance formulas; their signs exhibit the four regimes determined by \(d^2\), adjacent indicators are independent exactly at square sample sizes with counts \((N\pm\sqrt N)/2\), disjoint indicators are never independent, and summing the local covariance field recovers the classical runs variance.
limitations: The complete two-distance statement assumes N at least four; the adjacent formula alone remains valid for N equal to three.
Only binary fixed-count arrangements and pairwise dependence are classified.
